title: Refresh-token rotation invalidates the previous token
description:
When a client exchanges a refresh token for a new access token, the previous refresh token must be rejected on subsequent use. The rotation closes the replay window that exists in the current implementation.

## MoC

| # | AC | MoC | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Old refresh token is rejected after rotation | unit | jest test on TokenService.rotate |
| 2 | New refresh token works exactly once | unit | jest test on TokenService.rotate |
| 3 | Concurrent rotation attempts: second one fails | integ | concurrency test with two simulated clients |
acceptance_criteria:
- After rotation, the original refresh token returns 401 on use
- The newly issued refresh token can be exchanged exactly once
- Two concurrent rotation requests for the same token: one succeeds, the other returns 409

metadata.intent: Eliminate the replay window in refresh-token handling. Scope IN: rotation semantics in TokenService.rotate, persistence of issued/revoked state. Scope OUT: token expiry policy, OAuth consent flow, session management.
